title: The Neuroscience of Déjà Vu
question: Why do we sometimes feel certain we have already lived through a moment that is, in fact, entirely new?
summary: Roughly two-thirds of people experience déjà vu at some point, a brief, eerie conviction of having already experienced a novel situation. Once dismissed as mystical or a memory glitch, it is now studied through epilepsy patients, memory models, and controlled lab inductions, revealing it as a window into how the brain checks its own memories for accuracy.
